GOVERNING BOARD AGENDA SPECIAL MEETING – Board Actions Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. Duffy Community Center Multipurpose Room 5145 E. Fifth Street Tucson, AZ 85711 1. SCHEDULED EXECUTIVE MEETING - 4:30 p.m. 1.1 Roll Call 4:31 p.m. Board Member attendance was established via roll call. Those in attendance were Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah [via phone call]. Val Romero and Sadie Shaw were not present for roll call. 1.2 Motion to Convene Executive Meeting 4:31 p.m. Motion to go into executive meeting at this time to consider one or more of the following matters: Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Not Present at Vote: Val Romero and Sadie Shaw Motion Passed 3-0 1.3 Personnel Matters 1.4 Negotiations with Employee Groups 1.5 Adjourn Executive Meeting and Reconvene Regular Meeting 2. RECONVENE SPECIAL MEETING - CALL TO ORDER - 5:30 p.m. 2.1 Roll Call 5:39 p.m. Board member attendance was established via roll call. Those in attendance were Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, and Natalie Luna Rose. Ravi Shah was not present for roll call [arrived at 7:09 p.m.]. 2.2 Land Acknowledgement Statement 5:42 p.m. Isabella Muñoz, 3rd grader at Ochoa Community School, read the Land Acknowledgement Statement. 2.3 Pledge of Allegiance 5:43 p.m. Pledge led by Isabella Muñoz, 3rd grader at Ochoa Community School. 2.4 Agenda Adjustments
5:44 p.m. Dr. Trujillo recommended moving Board Activity Reports before Awards and Recognitions, move item 7.1 and all action items to follow Call to the Audience, and to move all consent items to follow item 9.3. By unanimous consent to move Board Activity Reports before Awards and Recognitions, move item 7.1 and all action items to follow Call to the Audience, and to move all consent items to follow item 9.3. 3. AWARDS AND RECOGNITIONS 3.1 Awards and Recognitions Details are available via the video and audio recordings on Diligent Community at https://tusd1-schooldesk.community.diligentoneplatform.com/Portal/ 5:54 p.m. Years of Service Recognition 5:58 p.m. Recessed for pictures. 5:59 p.m. Celebration of Life and Service - Joel Ireland The board held a moment of silence at 6:16 p.m. 6:17 p.m. Recess for performance by the Tucson High Magnet School Troubadours. 6:23 p.m. Recessed meeting. 6:31 p.m. Reconvened meeting. 4. BOARD MEMBER ACTIVITY REPORTS 4.1 Board Member Activity Reports 5:45 p.m. 5. CALL TO THE AUDIENCE 5.1 Guidelines to Address the Board 6:32 p.m. Point of order by Sadie Shaw that letter came in at 4:00 past the noon deadline. Point of Privilege by Natalie Luna Rose that she would be reading the comments. Natalie Luna Rose closed the Call to the Audience at 7:05 p.m. 6. CONSENT AGENDA (All items listed will be considered as a group with one motion. There will not be separate discussion of these items unless a Board Member so requests, in which case the item will be removed from the consent agenda and considered as a separate item.) 6.1 Approval of Consent Agenda Items 6.2 through 6.9 9:25 p.m.
Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.2 Approval of Supplemental Materials for Career and Technical Education Culinary Arts, Grades 9-12 Motion to approve Supplemental Materials for Career and Technical Education Culinary Arts, Grades 9-12 as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.3 Approval of Supplemental Materials for Career and Technical Education Engineering, Grades 9-12 Motion to approve Supplemental Materials for Career and Technical Education Engineering, Grades 9-12 as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.4 Approval of Course Proposal for Fine and Performing Arts, Conjunto, Grades 9-12 Motion to approve Course Proposal for Fine and Performing Arts, Conjunto, Grades 9-12 as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.5 Approval of the Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) between Tucson Unified School District (TUSD) and the Arizona Board of Regents (ABOR) for the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) Peer Coach Project for Various TUSD Schools, with Authorization for the Superintendent to Execute the Agreement
9:25 p.m. Motion to approve the Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) between Tucson Unified School District and Arizona Board of Regents (ABOR) for the FAFSA Peer Coach Project for Catalina High School, Cholla High School, Palo Verde High Magnet School, Pueblo High School, Rincon High School, Sabino High School, Tucson High Magnet School, and University High School, with authorization for the Superintendent to execute the agreement. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.6 Blanket Approval for High School and Middle School Participation in Fine and Performing Arts Non-Athletic Activities for the 2026-2027 School Year Motion to approve High School and Middle School Participation in Fine and Performing Arts Non-Athletic Activities for the 2026-2027 school year as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.7 Authorization for Governing Board Member(s) and Superintendent to travel on April 1-5, 2027, to attend the 2027 Annual National School Boards Association Conference on April 2-4, 2027, in Washington, DC Motion to approve Governing Board Member(s) and Superintendent to travel on April 1-5, 2027, to attend the 2027 Annual National School Boards Association Conference on April 2-4, 2027, in Washington, DC. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.8 Approval for Board Member Sadie Shaw to Attend the Arizona School Boards Association Law Conference in Addition to the Delegate Assembly, September 9-11, 2026, Scottsdale, Arizona Motion to approve Board Member Sadie Shaw to attend the Arizona School Boards Association Law Conference in addition to the Delegate Assembly from September 9-11, 2026 in Scottsdale, Arizona.
Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.9 Minutes of Tucson Unified School District Governing Board Meeting - August 11, 2026 Motion to approve the minutes of the Governing Board meeting held on August 11, 2026. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 7. PUBLIC HEARING 7.1 Public Hearing #2 for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-27 School Year 7:07 p.m. 8. ACTION ITEM(S) 8.1 Approval of the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-27 School Year 7:08 p.m. Motion to approve the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-27 school year. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 8.2 Approval to Appoint New Alternative Education Advisory Committee (AEAC) Members for a Four-year Term ending August 25, 2030 7:10 p.m. Motion to appoint the recommended candidates to serve a four-year term on the Alternative Education Advisory Committee. The board approved the appointments of Kimberly Elias and Lee Moyer to serve as members of the Alternative Education Advisory Committee. Moved by: Sadie Shaw; seconded by: Ravi Shah Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0
8.3 Approval to Appoint a New Bond Oversight Committee (BOC) Member for a Two-year Term ending August 25, 2028 7:12 p.m. Point of order from Sadie Shaw asking if current candidates can serve on our board committees. Jennifer Eckstrom clarified that he had rescinded his Governing Board candidacy. Motion to appoint the recommended candidate to serve a two-year term on the Bond Oversight Committee. The board approved the appointment of Lucas Verdugo to serve on the Bond Oversight Committee. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Ravi Shah Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 8.4 Approval to Procure Goods and Services for Quarter 1 FY26-27 and Quarter 2 FY26-27 Bond Project Priorities 7:13 p.m. Motion to grant authority to the Purchasing Director, in conjunction with the Bond Program Manager, to procure goods and services using approved TUSD and Cooperative Contracts for the next wave of bond projects, not to exceed + 20% Contingency, where single purchases may exceed $250,000.00 or for cumulative purchases with Cooperative Contract vendors in excess of $250,000.00. Moved by Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by Natalie Luna Rose Motion to divide the question by Ravi Shah; seconded by Sadie Shaw. Motion to approve the paving of the Sabino High School parking lots. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 Motion to approve the purchase of 20 new buses. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, and Natalie Luna Rose No: Ravi Shah Motion Passed 4-1 8.5 Approval to Award Request for Proposal (RFP) 27-021-TUSD1 – Board Agenda Management Software 7:33 p.m. Ravi Shah proposed to move item 9.3 for discussion next, followed by the rest of the study items, and then by the consent agenda. By unanimous consent to move item 9.3 for discussion next, followed by the rest of the study items, then by the consent agenda.
8:01 p.m. Recessed meeting. 8:11 p.m. Reconvened meeting. Motion to approve Request for Proposal (RFP) 27-021-TUSD1 – Board Agenda Management Software. Moved by: Val Romero; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 9. STUDY/ACTION ITEM(S) 9.1 Approval of Exceptional Education Tuition Schedule for Student Placement 9:31 p.m. 9:44 p.m. Point of order made by Sadie Shaw that this item was not properly agendized. Rob Ross clarified that all requirements were met. Motion to approve the Exceptional Education Tuition Schedule for Student Placement. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 9.2 Purchase and Sale Agreement with W/W GROUP, LLC, for 606 and 630 South Plumer Avenue, with Authorization for the Operations Program Manager to Execute the Agreement 10:11 p.m. Motion to approve the agreement with W/W Group LLC, for 606 and 630 South Plumer Avenue, with authorization for the Operations Program Manager to execute the agreement. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Ravi Shah Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 9.3 Reimagining Our Schools Together — A Community Engagement Plan for Elements of the Enrollment Stabilization Program 8:11 p.m. 8:38 p.m. Point of privilege by Sadie Shaw to apologize to Mrs. Hernández. Ravi Shah proposed moving consent items next followed by 9.1 and 9.2. By unanimous consent to move consent items next followed by 9.1 and 9.2. Motion to approve the timeline as presented. Moved by: Val Romero; seconded by: Ravi Shah Yes: Val Romero, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah
No: Sadie Shaw and Jennifer Eckstrom Motion Passed 3-2 10. FUTURE MEETING DATES and AGENDA ITEM(S) 10.1 Future Meeting Dates and Agenda Item(s) 10:12 p.m. Ravi Shah proposed adding two additional meetings, with the first on November 10th and the second on December 1st. By unanimous consent to add two additional meetings, with the first on November 10 th and the second on December 1 st . 11. ADJOURNMENT 11.1 Adjourn Meeting 10:13 p.m. Ravi Shah adjourned the meeting.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries regulated by the health department. Public use and driving under its influence remain illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to attend school or child care; Arizona allows medical and personal-belief exemptions with the state form.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Adults 21 and over who may legally own a firearm can carry it openly or concealed without a permit. An optional concealed-weapons permit exists, mainly for other states' recognition and certain locations.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — Arizona has a flat state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Department of Revenue.

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: Arizona expects new residents to get an Arizona license and register their vehicles promptly once residency is established — there is no fixed grace period, so the Motor Vehicle Division is an early errand.
facts.sourceOrg: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online or by mail at least 29 days before an election. Arizona voters show identification at the polls.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are billed by your county and fund schools, county, city, and district services; state law limits how fast a home's taxable value can grow, and qualifying seniors can apply to freeze their valuation.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. Arizona Game and Fish requires anyone 10 or older — resident or not — to hold a valid licence to take wildlife, fish included. People who live in Arizona pay less for one than visitors do.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: Arizona's constitution gives every person a fundamental right to abortion. Before the point a treating health professional judges the fetus could survive outside the womb, the state may restrict it only for a compelling health reason. After that point, it may not block an abortion that professional judges necessary to protect the pregnant person's life or health.

billSummary.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
billSummary.summary: A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries. Using it in public or driving under its influence remains illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need a set of routine immunizations to attend school or child care; New Jersey allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Carrying a handgun requires a Permit to Carry issued through the State Police, with training and application requirements; buying any firearm requires a purchaser identification card or pistol purchase permit.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — New Jersey has a graduated state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Division of Taxation.

facts.question: How long do I have to transfer my license and registration?
facts.answer: Within 60 days of moving in, or before your current license and registration expire — whichever comes first — through the Motor Vehicle Commission.

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online, by mail, or in person at least 21 days before an election. New Jersey mails every registered voter information about voting options each election.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are set and billed by your municipality and fund schools, county, and local services. The state's ANCHOR program pays a property-tax relief benefit to eligible homeowners and renters.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Jersey law requires a licence to hunt or trap at any age, and anyone over 16 needs one to fish the state's fresh waters with a rod and line. Saltwater fishing is registered separately rather than licensed.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 23:3-1 (Licence for hunting, fishing, trapping)

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Jersey law states a fundamental right to choose whether to carry a pregnancy, to give birth, or to end one. The Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act sets no time limit and requires no waiting period.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 10:7-2 (Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act)

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Recreational marijuana is not legal. Possessing three-quarters of an ounce or less is a civil violation (a fine, not a crime), and a state-run therapeutic cannabis program serves qualifying patients.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to enroll in school or child care; New Hampshire allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows anyone who may legally own a handgun to carry it openly or concealed without a license. An optional pistol/revolver license exists, mainly for carrying in other states that honor it.
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: No — New Hampshire does not tax wages, and its separate tax on interest and dividends was repealed effective 2025. There is also no state sales tax.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: New residents have 60 days after establishing residency to register vehicles and get a New Hampshire driver's license. Registration runs through your town clerk plus the DMV.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Division of Motor Vehicles
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register with your town or city clerk ahead of time, or at the polls on election day itself. Bring proof of who you are, your age, your citizenship, and where you live.
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are the main way New Hampshire towns and schools are funded, set town by town; the annual town meeting votes the budget that drives the rate. Credits and exemptions (veterans, elderly, disabled) run through your town.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Hampshire law says nobody may fish, hunt or trap in the state without first getting a valid licence, and it has to be carried while you are doing it. The same chapter sets out the exceptions, including some for young people.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows abortion up to 24 weeks of pregnancy. From 24 weeks a provider may not perform one except in a medical emergency, and must first determine the likely gestational age. There is no time limit written into state law before that point.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire RSA 329:44 (Fetal Life Protection Act — Prohibition)

Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, July 28, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 7/29/2026

Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, July 28, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 7/27/2026

meetings.minutes: Per the Board's posted meeting-summary report (full minutes post after approval): the Board appointed Jorge Soto as Pima County Treasurer (4–1, one abstention) after a first motion for a different candidate died without a second. It removed all five members of the county's Industrial Development Authority board without cause, approved a new structure for that authority, and elected new members. It also approved the River Overlook rezoning and comprehensive-plan amendment on West River Road (5–0) and two cell-tower permits, updated the county's air-quality code to match current federal rules, denied a wholesale liquor license on East Cabeza De Vaca Street (zoning there does not allow wholesale), and — sitting as the Library District board — accepted a $7,500 grant for a local-news pilot program (4–1), among other business.

Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, September 8, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, September 8, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 9/1/2026

GOVERNING BOARD AGENDA SPECIAL MEETING – Board Actions Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. Duffy Community Center Multipurpose Room 5145 E. Fifth Street Tucson, AZ 85711 1. SCHEDULED EXECUTIVE MEETING - 4:30 p.m. 1.1 Roll Call 4:31 p.m. Board Member attendance was established via roll call. Those in attendance were Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah [via phone call]. Val Romero and Sadie Shaw were not present for roll call. 1.2 Motion to Convene Executive Meeting 4:31 p.m. Motion to go into executive meeting at this time to consider one or more of the following matters: Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Not Present at Vote: Val Romero and Sadie Shaw Motion Passed 3-0 1.3 Personnel Matters 1.4 Negotiations with Employee Groups 1.5 Adjourn Executive Meeting and Reconvene Regular Meeting 2. RECONVENE SPECIAL MEETING - CALL TO ORDER - 5:30 p.m. 2.1 Roll Call 5:39 p.m. Board member attendance was established via roll call. Those in attendance were Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, and Natalie Luna Rose. Ravi Shah was not present for roll call [arrived at 7:09 p.m.]. 2.2 Land Acknowledgement Statement 5:42 p.m. Isabella Muñoz, 3rd grader at Ochoa Community School, read the Land Acknowledgement Statement. 2.3 Pledge of Allegiance 5:43 p.m. Pledge led by Isabella Muñoz, 3rd grader at Ochoa Community School. 2.4 Agenda Adjustments
5:44 p.m. Dr. Trujillo recommended moving Board Activity Reports before Awards and Recognitions, move item 7.1 and all action items to follow Call to the Audience, and to move all consent items to follow item 9.3. By unanimous consent to move Board Activity Reports before Awards and Recognitions, move item 7.1 and all action items to follow Call to the Audience, and to move all consent items to follow item 9.3. 3. AWARDS AND RECOGNITIONS 3.1 Awards and Recognitions Details are available via the video and audio recordings on Diligent Community at https://tusd1-schooldesk.community.diligentoneplatform.com/Portal/ 5:54 p.m. Years of Service Recognition 5:58 p.m. Recessed for pictures. 5:59 p.m. Celebration of Life and Service - Joel Ireland The board held a moment of silence at 6:16 p.m. 6:17 p.m. Recess for performance by the Tucson High Magnet School Troubadours. 6:23 p.m. Recessed meeting. 6:31 p.m. Reconvened meeting. 4. BOARD MEMBER ACTIVITY REPORTS 4.1 Board Member Activity Reports 5:45 p.m. 5. CALL TO THE AUDIENCE 5.1 Guidelines to Address the Board 6:32 p.m. Point of order by Sadie Shaw that letter came in at 4:00 past the noon deadline. Point of Privilege by Natalie Luna Rose that she would be reading the comments. Natalie Luna Rose closed the Call to the Audience at 7:05 p.m. 6. CONSENT AGENDA (All items listed will be considered as a group with one motion. There will not be separate discussion of these items unless a Board Member so requests, in which case the item will be removed from the consent agenda and considered as a separate item.) 6.1 Approval of Consent Agenda Items 6.2 through 6.9 9:25 p.m.
Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.2 Approval of Supplemental Materials for Career and Technical Education Culinary Arts, Grades 9-12 Motion to approve Supplemental Materials for Career and Technical Education Culinary Arts, Grades 9-12 as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.3 Approval of Supplemental Materials for Career and Technical Education Engineering, Grades 9-12 Motion to approve Supplemental Materials for Career and Technical Education Engineering, Grades 9-12 as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.4 Approval of Course Proposal for Fine and Performing Arts, Conjunto, Grades 9-12 Motion to approve Course Proposal for Fine and Performing Arts, Conjunto, Grades 9-12 as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.5 Approval of the Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) between Tucson Unified School District (TUSD) and the Arizona Board of Regents (ABOR) for the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) Peer Coach Project for Various TUSD Schools, with Authorization for the Superintendent to Execute the Agreement
9:25 p.m. Motion to approve the Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) between Tucson Unified School District and Arizona Board of Regents (ABOR) for the FAFSA Peer Coach Project for Catalina High School, Cholla High School, Palo Verde High Magnet School, Pueblo High School, Rincon High School, Sabino High School, Tucson High Magnet School, and University High School, with authorization for the Superintendent to execute the agreement. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.6 Blanket Approval for High School and Middle School Participation in Fine and Performing Arts Non-Athletic Activities for the 2026-2027 School Year Motion to approve High School and Middle School Participation in Fine and Performing Arts Non-Athletic Activities for the 2026-2027 school year as presented. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.7 Authorization for Governing Board Member(s) and Superintendent to travel on April 1-5, 2027, to attend the 2027 Annual National School Boards Association Conference on April 2-4, 2027, in Washington, DC Motion to approve Governing Board Member(s) and Superintendent to travel on April 1-5, 2027, to attend the 2027 Annual National School Boards Association Conference on April 2-4, 2027, in Washington, DC. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.8 Approval for Board Member Sadie Shaw to Attend the Arizona School Boards Association Law Conference in Addition to the Delegate Assembly, September 9-11, 2026, Scottsdale, Arizona Motion to approve Board Member Sadie Shaw to attend the Arizona School Boards Association Law Conference in addition to the Delegate Assembly from September 9-11, 2026 in Scottsdale, Arizona.
Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 6.9 Minutes of Tucson Unified School District Governing Board Meeting - August 11, 2026 Motion to approve the minutes of the Governing Board meeting held on August 11, 2026. Dr. Trujillo recommends approval of the Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9. Val Romero requested to pull item 6.5 for discussion. Resolution: Consent Agenda items 6.2 through 6.9 were approved. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 7. PUBLIC HEARING 7.1 Public Hearing #2 for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-27 School Year 7:07 p.m. 8. ACTION ITEM(S) 8.1 Approval of the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-27 School Year 7:08 p.m. Motion to approve the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-27 school year. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 8.2 Approval to Appoint New Alternative Education Advisory Committee (AEAC) Members for a Four-year Term ending August 25, 2030 7:10 p.m. Motion to appoint the recommended candidates to serve a four-year term on the Alternative Education Advisory Committee. The board approved the appointments of Kimberly Elias and Lee Moyer to serve as members of the Alternative Education Advisory Committee. Moved by: Sadie Shaw; seconded by: Ravi Shah Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0
8.3 Approval to Appoint a New Bond Oversight Committee (BOC) Member for a Two-year Term ending August 25, 2028 7:12 p.m. Point of order from Sadie Shaw asking if current candidates can serve on our board committees. Jennifer Eckstrom clarified that he had rescinded his Governing Board candidacy. Motion to appoint the recommended candidate to serve a two-year term on the Bond Oversight Committee. The board approved the appointment of Lucas Verdugo to serve on the Bond Oversight Committee. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Ravi Shah Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 8.4 Approval to Procure Goods and Services for Quarter 1 FY26-27 and Quarter 2 FY26-27 Bond Project Priorities 7:13 p.m. Motion to grant authority to the Purchasing Director, in conjunction with the Bond Program Manager, to procure goods and services using approved TUSD and Cooperative Contracts for the next wave of bond projects, not to exceed + 20% Contingency, where single purchases may exceed $250,000.00 or for cumulative purchases with Cooperative Contract vendors in excess of $250,000.00. Moved by Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by Natalie Luna Rose Motion to divide the question by Ravi Shah; seconded by Sadie Shaw. Motion to approve the paving of the Sabino High School parking lots. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 Motion to approve the purchase of 20 new buses. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, and Natalie Luna Rose No: Ravi Shah Motion Passed 4-1 8.5 Approval to Award Request for Proposal (RFP) 27-021-TUSD1 – Board Agenda Management Software 7:33 p.m. Ravi Shah proposed to move item 9.3 for discussion next, followed by the rest of the study items, and then by the consent agenda. By unanimous consent to move item 9.3 for discussion next, followed by the rest of the study items, then by the consent agenda.
8:01 p.m. Recessed meeting. 8:11 p.m. Reconvened meeting. Motion to approve Request for Proposal (RFP) 27-021-TUSD1 – Board Agenda Management Software. Moved by: Val Romero; seconded by: Jennifer Eckstrom Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 9. STUDY/ACTION ITEM(S) 9.1 Approval of Exceptional Education Tuition Schedule for Student Placement 9:31 p.m. 9:44 p.m. Point of order made by Sadie Shaw that this item was not properly agendized. Rob Ross clarified that all requirements were met. Motion to approve the Exceptional Education Tuition Schedule for Student Placement. Moved by: Ravi Shah; seconded by: Natalie Luna Rose Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 9.2 Purchase and Sale Agreement with W/W GROUP, LLC, for 606 and 630 South Plumer Avenue, with Authorization for the Operations Program Manager to Execute the Agreement 10:11 p.m. Motion to approve the agreement with W/W Group LLC, for 606 and 630 South Plumer Avenue, with authorization for the Operations Program Manager to execute the agreement. Moved by: Jennifer Eckstrom; seconded by: Ravi Shah Yes: Val Romero, Sadie Shaw, Jennifer Eckstrom, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah Motion Passed 5-0 9.3 Reimagining Our Schools Together — A Community Engagement Plan for Elements of the Enrollment Stabilization Program 8:11 p.m. 8:38 p.m. Point of privilege by Sadie Shaw to apologize to Mrs. Hernández. Ravi Shah proposed moving consent items next followed by 9.1 and 9.2. By unanimous consent to move consent items next followed by 9.1 and 9.2. Motion to approve the timeline as presented. Moved by: Val Romero; seconded by: Ravi Shah Yes: Val Romero, Natalie Luna Rose, and Ravi Shah
No: Sadie Shaw and Jennifer Eckstrom Motion Passed 3-2 10. FUTURE MEETING DATES and AGENDA ITEM(S) 10.1 Future Meeting Dates and Agenda Item(s) 10:12 p.m. Ravi Shah proposed adding two additional meetings, with the first on November 10th and the second on December 1st. By unanimous consent to add two additional meetings, with the first on November 10 th and the second on December 1 st . 11. ADJOURNMENT 11.1 Adjourn Meeting 10:13 p.m. Ravi Shah adjourned the meeting.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries regulated by the health department. Public use and driving under its influence remain illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to attend school or child care; Arizona allows medical and personal-belief exemptions with the state form.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Adults 21 and over who may legally own a firearm can carry it openly or concealed without a permit. An optional concealed-weapons permit exists, mainly for other states' recognition and certain locations.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — Arizona has a flat state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Department of Revenue.

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: Arizona expects new residents to get an Arizona license and register their vehicles promptly once residency is established — there is no fixed grace period, so the Motor Vehicle Division is an early errand.
facts.sourceOrg: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online or by mail at least 29 days before an election. Arizona voters show identification at the polls.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are billed by your county and fund schools, county, city, and district services; state law limits how fast a home's taxable value can grow, and qualifying seniors can apply to freeze their valuation.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. Arizona Game and Fish requires anyone 10 or older — resident or not — to hold a valid licence to take wildlife, fish included. People who live in Arizona pay less for one than visitors do.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: Arizona's constitution gives every person a fundamental right to abortion. Before the point a treating health professional judges the fetus could survive outside the womb, the state may restrict it only for a compelling health reason. After that point, it may not block an abortion that professional judges necessary to protect the pregnant person's life or health.

billSummary.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
billSummary.summary: A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing.

The public is invited to attend in person or to view the meeting by following the link below or by calling in to the phone number listed below the link. Public comments are welcome in person or by submitting written comments to the Clerk of the Board, which may be read or summarized during the public portion of the meeting. Written comments may be submitted via email with the subject line “Public Comment”’ to the Clerk of the Board, Michele Reilly at mreilly@co.morris.nj.us or by mail addressed to Michele Reilly, Clerk of the Board, Morris County Board of County Commissioners, PO Box 900, Morristown, NJ 07963-0900. Emailed comments must be received at least eight (8) hours prior to the meeting. Mailed comments must be received by 4:00 p.m. the day before the meeting. meetings.minutes: The Board approved the minutes of its July 8 meetings and three permission requests, including street closings for Boonton's Labor Day parade. It adopted resolutions including an amendment extending the historic-preservation easement on the Pompton Plains Railroad Station to 2056. Two of the seven commissioners were absent. During public comment, residents raised the county's ADA grievance process and asked for updates on a homicide investigation. The Board opened with condolences on the death of longtime Boonton official Cy Wekilsky, among other business.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries. Using it in public or driving under its influence remains illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need a set of routine immunizations to attend school or child care; New Jersey allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Carrying a handgun requires a Permit to Carry issued through the State Police, with training and application requirements; buying any firearm requires a purchaser identification card or pistol purchase permit.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — New Jersey has a graduated state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Division of Taxation.

facts.question: How long do I have to transfer my license and registration?
facts.answer: Within 60 days of moving in, or before your current license and registration expire — whichever comes first — through the Motor Vehicle Commission.

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online, by mail, or in person at least 21 days before an election. New Jersey mails every registered voter information about voting options each election.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are set and billed by your municipality and fund schools, county, and local services. The state's ANCHOR program pays a property-tax relief benefit to eligible homeowners and renters.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Jersey law requires a licence to hunt or trap at any age, and anyone over 16 needs one to fish the state's fresh waters with a rod and line. Saltwater fishing is registered separately rather than licensed.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 23:3-1 (Licence for hunting, fishing, trapping)

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Jersey law states a fundamental right to choose whether to carry a pregnancy, to give birth, or to end one. The Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act sets no time limit and requires no waiting period.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 10:7-2 (Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act)

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Recreational marijuana is not legal. Possessing three-quarters of an ounce or less is a civil violation (a fine, not a crime), and a state-run therapeutic cannabis program serves qualifying patients.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to enroll in school or child care; New Hampshire allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows anyone who may legally own a handgun to carry it openly or concealed without a license. An optional pistol/revolver license exists, mainly for carrying in other states that honor it.
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: No — New Hampshire does not tax wages, and its separate tax on interest and dividends was repealed effective 2025. There is also no state sales tax.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: New residents have 60 days after establishing residency to register vehicles and get a New Hampshire driver's license. Registration runs through your town clerk plus the DMV.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Division of Motor Vehicles
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register with your town or city clerk ahead of time, or at the polls on election day itself. Bring proof of who you are, your age, your citizenship, and where you live.
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are the main way New Hampshire towns and schools are funded, set town by town; the annual town meeting votes the budget that drives the rate. Credits and exemptions (veterans, elderly, disabled) run through your town.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Hampshire law says nobody may fish, hunt or trap in the state without first getting a valid licence, and it has to be carried while you are doing it. The same chapter sets out the exceptions, including some for young people.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows abortion up to 24 weeks of pregnancy. From 24 weeks a provider may not perform one except in a medical emergency, and must first determine the likely gestational age. There is no time limit written into state law before that point.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire RSA 329:44 (Fetal Life Protection Act — Prohibition)
